## Summary

The bug in `split_evenly()` was caused by swapping the return values from `divmod()` - the code assigned the remainder to `extra` and the quotient to `base`, when it should have been the opposite. Swapping the variable names in the `divmod()` assignment from `extra, base = divmod(cents, parts)` to `base, extra = divmod(cents, parts)` fixes the issue so that amounts are correctly split and add up to the original total.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `due_date` function in `invoicer/dates.py` where NET payment terms were calculating the due date by subtracting 1 from the number of days, causing invoices to be due one day too early. The fix was to remove the `- 1` operation so that NET 30 now correctly adds 30 calendar days from the invoice issue date.

Perfect! All tests pass. Here's a summary of the fix:

**The `tax_for()` function now wraps its result with `to_money()` to ensure the calculated tax is always rounded to exactly two decimal places, fixing the issue where small tax amounts would have more than two decimal places.**

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `apply_coupon` function in `invoicer/discounts.py` on line 22, which was using `max()` instead of `min()`. This caused large coupons to override the subtotal instead of being capped at it. Changed `max(to_money(amount), subtotal)` to `min(to_money(amount), subtotal)` to ensure the discount amount never exceeds the order subtotal.

Perfect! All tests pass now. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `Invoice.add()` method's quantity validation: it only checked for negative quantities (`< 0`) but didn't reject zero quantities. The fix was to change the condition from `line.quantity < 0` to `line.quantity <= 0` to reject both zero and negative quantities with the error message "quantity must be positive".

Perfect! All tests pass. The bug has been fixed.

## Summary

The bug was that line descriptions imported from CSV were not being stripped of whitespace, while all other fields (invoice number, category, unit price) were. I fixed it by adding `.strip()` to the `description` field on line 29 of `invoicer/csv_import.py`, ensuring that descriptions imported from CSV have leading and trailing spaces removed, consistent with the handling of other fields.

Excellent! The fix is complete. 

## Summary

Fixed the `total_receivable()` method in `invoicer/ledger.py` to only sum positive balances (customers who owe us money) instead of including negative balances (customers we owe money to), by changing the condition from `if b != 0` to `if b > 0` on line 136.

Excellent! The fix is confirmed. The change on line 130 from `e.on < as_of` to `e.on <= as_of` now includes entries posted on the `as_of` date itself in the balance calculation.

## Summary

The bug in the `balance()` method was fixed by changing the comparison operator from `<` to `<=` on line 130 of `invoicer/ledger.py`, so that entries posted on the `as_of` date are now included in the balance calculation instead of being excluded.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `statement()` method in `invoicer/ledger.py` on line 208. The header line was using the format `"Statement: {customer}"` when it should have been `"Statement for {customer}"`. I changed the colon to "for" to match the expected format in the test.
